skill.name: building-chat-interfaces
skill.description: Guides building AI chat interfaces that connect React ChatKit frontends to Python backends with authentication, context metadata, persistence, and Next.js proxy patterns.
skill.summary: Build authenticated ChatKit interfaces with custom backends, context injection, persistence, and proxy-based token handling.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, JavaScript template literals, public configuration examples, and documented ChatKit network calls. A real semantic risk remains: the MCP authentication guidance places access tokens into model prompt context, which can expose credentials through prompt injection, logs, or unintended model output.

remediation.issue: Access tokens are embedded in the model prompt for MCP tool authentication.
remediation.suggestion: Replace prompt-carried tokens with backend-mediated tool calls, short-lived server sessions, or scoped opaque handles resolved server-side.

remediation.issue: Database URL examples assume the environment variable exists before calling string methods.
remediation.suggestion: Validate required environment variables at startup and fail with a clear server-side configuration error.

remediation.issue: Examples forward page context and selected text to a chat backend.
remediation.suggestion: Document consent, minimization, and redaction requirements before sending page metadata or selected content.

semantic_findings.title: Access Token Included in Model Prompt
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends placing an access token in the system prompt and instructing the model to include it in MCP tool calls. This can expose bearer tokens through model context, logs, prompt injection, or unintended output.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 291-307 directly format access_token into SYSTEM_PROMPT and require it for any MCP tool call. This is a clear credential exposure design risk, not a scanner pattern duplicate.

content.value_statement: Teams need chat interfaces that connect UI, auth, context, and backend agents without fragile glue code. This skill gives reusable ChatKit patterns for React, Next.js, Python backends, and secure request routing.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to extend ChatKitServer with a custom Python agent response flow.
Shows useChatKit configuration with custom fetch handling for auth and context metadata.
Documents a Next.js API route proxy for httpOnly cookie authentication.
Covers page context extraction and selected text chat handoff patterns.
Shows script loading detection for ChatKit web components in React and Next.js.
Includes a verification script that checks required reference files are present.
limitations: Examples assume OpenAI ChatKit, React or Next.js, and a Python backend.
The skill provides patterns, not a complete production application.
Code samples need adaptation for each auth provider, database, and deployment target.
The MCP token-in-prompt guidance should be replaced before production use.

use_cases.title: Add a Custom Chat Backend
use_cases.description: Connect a ChatKit frontend to a Python agent backend with conversation history and request context.

use_cases.title: Protect Chat Requests
use_cases.description: Route chat calls through authenticated fetch handlers and Next.js proxies for cookie-based sessions.

use_cases.title: Review Chat Architecture
use_cases.description: Check where user context, page data, scripts, and credentials move through a ChatKit integration.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a ChatKit Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a first authenticated chat interface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the building-chat-interfaces skill to plan a basic ChatKit architecture for a React frontend and Python backend. Include auth, context, persistence, and deployment notes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Authenticated Fetch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the building-chat-interfaces skill to design a useChatKit custom fetch flow. It should require login, add user context, and avoid exposing secrets in browser code.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Next.js Proxy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the building-chat-interfaces skill to outline a Next.js API route proxy for httpOnly cookie auth. Cover request forwarding, SSE streaming, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review Credential Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the building-chat-interfaces skill to review a ChatKit integration for credential exposure. Pay special attention to MCP auth, prompts, logs, and page context.

output_examples.input: Plan an authenticated ChatKit integration for a product dashboard.
output: A frontend flow using useChatKit with login checks and context metadata.
A backend flow using ChatKitServer with user-scoped request context.
A deployment checklist for script loading, persistence, and auth boundaries.

output_examples.input: Review a Next.js ChatKit proxy design that uses httpOnly cookies.
output: A proxy responsibility summary covering cookie reads, Authorization forwarding, and SSE streaming.
A list of risks around missing auth checks, leaked tokens, and incorrect backend routes.
Concrete changes to keep credentials server-side and minimize forwarded context.

output_examples.input: Improve a ChatKit widget that sends selected page text to the assistant.
output: A user interaction flow for selection, chat opening, and message handoff.
Privacy notes for consent, redaction, and limiting page metadata.
Implementation checkpoints for script readiness and authenticated requests.

best_practices: Keep access tokens server-side and use proxies or scoped session handles for authenticated tool calls.
Scope all ChatKit storage and backend operations by authenticated user identity.
Send only the page context required for the current chat task.
anti_patterns: Putting bearer tokens or database credentials into model prompts.
Reading private environment variables from browser code.
Forwarding chat traffic through a proxy that does not enforce authentication.

faq.question: What kind of chat interface does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets authenticated AI chat interfaces that use ChatKit with custom backend agents and context-aware requests.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation patterns, reference snippets, and architecture guidance that must be adapted to a real app.

faq.question: Can it help with httpOnly cookie authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains a Next.js server-side proxy pattern for reading cookies and forwarding authorized chat requests.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What security issue should users review first?
faq.answer: Users should replace the token-in-prompt MCP authentication guidance with server-side credential handling before production use.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it for simple unauthenticated chatbots that do not need custom agents, persistence, proxies, or context injection.
